text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants (exact, whitespace/case, punctuation, changed quantity, added negation, removed negation, reordered, paraphrase).

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2023, the Kesa Valley Savings Initiative supported 42 village savings and loan groups across Mbaruti and Lowani districts. Total member savings reached 61,400 shillings, an increase of 18% on the previous quarter. Field officers recorded that women made up seventy percent of active members. Group treasurers trained new members in record keeping. Loan repayment remained strong, with three groups reporting full repayment ahead of schedule. However, two groups in Lowani did not hold their share-out meetings because of flooding on access roads. Officers visited each group at least twice during the period, and no cases of fund misappropriation were reported. The programme will add eight new groups before the end of March 2024.

passages.source_passage: Between January and June 2024, the Tamsin Ridge Paralegal Network handled 316 cases through its six community advice desks. Land and inheritance disputes accounted for 41% of new cases, followed by domestic violence and unpaid wages. Paralegals referred twenty-two complex cases to partner lawyers in Orvane town. Clients were not charged any fees for advice or accompaniment to court. Average waiting time for a first appointment fell from nine days to four days. The network's mobile clinic did not reach the two northern wards because its vehicle was under repair for most of May. Paralegals supported elders in drafting written mediation agreements.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Sabelo Coast Net Campaign found that 84,000 long-lasting insecticidal nets had been distributed by September 2022, against a target of 110,000. Household surveys in Kirembe and Dunasi showed that 67% of children under five had slept under a net the previous night. Community mobilisers taught households to hang nets correctly. Evaluators noted that nets were not consistently used during the hot season, when many families sleep outdoors. Stock-outs at two distribution points delayed delivery by about three weeks. No damaged nets were replaced during the first year, and the replacement scheme has not yet started.

passages.source_passage: In the Haripura block of Sundar Valley district, only 38% of births in 2021 took place in a health facility. The nearest functioning labour room is often more than 25 kilometres from outlying hamlets, and many roads are not passable during the monsoon. Since 2019, the Navjeevan Health Trust has run monthly outreach camps from four clinics. Auxiliary nurse midwives visit pregnant women at home and record danger signs. Yet newborns are rarely examined within the first two days, and in a recent audit nine of every ten home births had no postnatal check. This proposal seeks support to extend outreach to thirty additional villages.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Lindo Plains WASH project aimed to complete 24 boreholes by December 2023. As of this update, 19 boreholes are operational and serve roughly 11,500 people. Five sites were delayed because the drilling contractor did not secure permits in time. The district water office audits the contractor every quarter. Latrine construction has gone faster than expected, with 640 household latrines built against a target of 500. Water committees collect a monthly fee of two hundred kwacha from each household. We have not yet seen a measurable drop in diarrhoea cases at Mpata clinic, although data for only six months are available. Management recommends extending the project by one quarter.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Ubuntu Hills Home-Based Care Programme covered visits made between March 2021 and February 2022. Trained caregivers conducted 7,820 home visits to 412 clients living with HIV. Viral load suppression among enrolled clients rose from 71% to 86% over the period. Caregivers accompanied clients to the district clinic when transport was available. Evaluators found that caregivers did not receive refresher training after their first year, and several had never been supervised in person. Stipends were paid late in four of the twelve months. Clients consistently described the visits as respectful, and none reported disclosure of their status without consent.

passages.source_passage: Across Merrowfield province, an estimated 2,300 children live in residential institutions, and a 2022 government review found that at least 60% of them have a living parent. Many were placed during the drought years without any assessment of family circumstances. Since 2018, the Hearthway Children's Alliance has recruited and trained 85 foster families. Social workers trace relatives through churches, markets and radio announcements. Of the 143 children traced last year, 97 were reunified safely, and no reunified child has returned to an institution. However, the Alliance does not currently have staff in the three eastern districts, where institutional placements are rising fastest.

passages.source_passage: This update covers case management in Kaliro Settlement Camp for the quarter ending 30 September 2024. Caseworkers opened 534 new protection cases, of which 29% involved unaccompanied or separated children. The average caseload per worker rose to 61, well above the agreed ceiling of forty. Two experienced caseworkers resigned in August and have not been replaced. Survivors of gender-based violence were referred to the camp health post within 72 hours in most cases. We did not record any incidents of refoulement during the quarter. The protection team assisted camp leaders in revising the safe shelter guidelines.

passages.source_passage: Wanjala District in the western highlands has a population of about 380,000 but only 14 qualified doctors. Since 2016, the Mlima Health Partnership has supported 260 community health workers, each responsible for roughly 100 households. Community health workers screen children for malnutrition and refer severe cases to health centres. In 2023, they identified 1,140 children with acute malnutrition, and 88% of referred children completed treatment. However, the workers are not salaried, and turnover reached one in five last year. Many have never received a replacement bicycle or medical kit since their initial training. Stable funding would allow the district to retain experienced workers.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation reviewed the Riverbend Listening Circles service from its launch in April 2022 to October 2023. Lay counsellors delivered 3,460 sessions to 590 adults experiencing distress after the Oshava floods. Average scores on the wellbeing scale improved by 32% between intake and the eighth session. Two clinical psychologists supervised the counsellors in weekly case reviews. Evaluators noted that men were not well represented, making up only a quarter of clients. Referral pathways to the district hospital were never formalised, and some clients waited over a month for psychiatric review. Most participants said they would recommend the circles to a neighbour.
